knowledge:
- key_parameters: ddsList=A named list of datasets to compare, where each element can be a DESeqDataSet, matrix, or data.frame ;; outputFile=The filename of the generated report (e.g., "countsim_report.html") ;; outputDir=The directory where the output report and files will be saved ;; outputFormat=The format of the report, either "html_document" or "pdf_document" ;; savePlots=Logical, if TRUE, saves an .rds file containing the individual ggplot objects ;; calculateStatistics=Logical, if TRUE, performs quantitative pairwise comparisons (Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Wald-Wolfowitz runs tests) ;; permutationPvalues=Logical, if TRUE, uses label permutation to evaluate statistical significance (significantly increases runtime) ;; subsampleSize=The number of observations to subsample for calculating statistics to speed up computation
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to compare the properties (e.g., dispersion, correlations, count distributions) of multiple count datasets, particularly when validating synthetic count data against a real reference dataset.
- pitfalls: Providing datasets as a matrix or data.frame instead of a DESeqDataSet forces the assumption that all samples are replicates (design ~1), which ignores experimental design in dispersion calculations. Setting permutationPvalues = TRUE significantly increases runtime. Setting savePlots = TRUE can generate very large .rds files if datasets contain many samples or features.

workflows.name: count_dataset_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare characteristic features across multiple count datasets, generate a comprehensive HTML/PDF report, and export individual figures.
input: countsimExample (named list of DESeqDataSet, matrix, or data.frame objects containing count matrices and sample metadata)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the countsimQC and DESeq2 libraries.
2. Prepare the input datasets as a named list of DESeqDataSet, matrix, or data.frame objects.
3. Run countsimQCReport to perform statistical comparisons and generate the HTML/PDF report.
4. Read the saved ggplot objects from the generated RDS file and export individual figures using generateIndividualPlots.
workflows.code:
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(countsimQC)
  library(DESeq2)
})

data(countsimExample)
countsimExample
countsimExample <- lapply(countsimExample, function(cse) {
  cse[seq_len(1500), ]
})

tempDir <- tempdir()
countsimQCReport(ddsList = countsimExample, outputFile = "countsim_report.html",
                 outputDir = tempDir, outputFormat = "html_document", 
                 showCode = FALSE, forceOverwrite = TRUE,
                 savePlots = TRUE, description = "This is my test report.", 
                 maxNForCorr = 25, maxNForDisp = Inf, 
                 calculateStatistics = TRUE, subsampleSize = 25,
                 kfrac = 0.01, kmin = 5, 
                 permutationPvalues = FALSE, nPermutations = NULL)

ggplots <- readRDS(file.path(tempDir, "countsim_report_ggplots.rds"))
if (!dir.exists(file.path(tempDir, "figures"))) {
  dir.create(file.path(tempDir, "figures"))
}
generateIndividualPlots(ggplots, device = "pdf", nDatasets = 3, 
                        outputDir = file.path(tempDir, "figures"))
